commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

# S-116: Weekly sleep summary

**As a** NightJar user,
**I want** a summary of my last seven nights,
**so I can** see how consistent my routine has been.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Traces to | [BR-07](../requirements/BR-07.md) |
| Status | Ready for development (no code yet) |
| Owner | Product (fictional: Priya N.) |

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: The summary covers the seven nights before today: the "night of" dates from
  seven days ago up to and including last night, using the user's current time zone for
  "today". A night belongs to its "night of" date as shown in the diary (a 00:15 bedtime
  on Sunday counts as Saturday night).
- **AC2**: It shows how many nights were logged in that window, the average time asleep,
  and the usual bedtime for those nights.
- **AC3**: Average time asleep is the mean of the nights' durations, shown in hours and
  minutes rounded to the nearest 5 minutes, for example "7 h 25 min".
- **AC4**: The usual bedtime is the median local bedtime of the nights in the window,
  each night in its own time zone. Bedtimes on both sides of midnight are handled as they
  are for the nudge (23:30 and 00:30 are one hour apart).
- **AC5**: With fewer than 3 nights logged in the window, no figures are shown and the
  summary says "Log at least 3 nights this week to see your summary."
- **AC6**: All summary wording passes the claims check.
- **Non-functional**: Durations are real elapsed time, so a night that crosses a
  daylight-saving change is an hour shorter or longer on the clock. The summary sits on
  the home page, above the sleep diary.

content.content:
# Claims policy

NightJar is a wellness product. It may help people relax and keep a regular
routine. It may not claim to diagnose, treat or cure any condition.

The source of truth is [`claims/register.yaml`](../claims/register.yaml), owned by
Regulatory & Brand (fictional). It holds:

- **approved_phrases**: wellness language we may use ("wind down", "relax",
  "build a consistent bedtime routine", ...).
- **nudge_copy**: the only templates the bedtime nudge may show (S-114 AC4).
- **banned**: regular expressions for disease and treatment claims ("insomnia",
  "sleep apnea", "treat", "cure", "diagnose", "anxiety disorder", "prescribe",
  "clinically proven").

## How it is enforced

- `claims.check_text(text) -> list[Violation]` is case-insensitive and uses word
  boundaries ("retreat" is fine, "treat" is not).
- Nudge copy is picked only from `nudge_copy`.
- Every coach answer goes through `check_text`. If it finds a violation, the user
  sees a safe fallback instead, and the violation is logged and written to the trace.

## Known trade-offs

The check is deliberately strict. "Treat yourself to a bath" is flagged. That is
acceptable: a false positive shows the fallback; a false negative ships a disease claim.

Changing the register needs Regulatory review. Don't edit it to make a test pass.
# S-114: Bedtime wind-down nudge

**As a** NightJar user,
**I get** a gentle wind-down nudge before my usual bedtime,
**so I can** start relaxing.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Traces to | [BR-07](../requirements/BR-07.md) -> [PR-21](../requirements/PR-21.md) |
| Code | `src/nightjar/nudge.py`, `src/nightjar/sleep_window.py` |
| Tests | see [traceability](../traceability.md) |

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: With 7+ nights of data, the nudge is scheduled 45 min before the usual
  bedtime, in the user's current local time.
- **AC2**: After a time zone change, the nudge follows the new local time from the next day.
- **AC3**: During the user's quiet hours / Do Not Disturb, the nudge is delivered
  silently (flag), not skipped.
- **AC4**: Nudge copy uses only phrases from the claims register.
- **Edge**: Fewer than 7 nights -> no nudge.
- **Non-functional**: Correct across daylight-saving transitions (spring forward and
  fall back) in America/Toronto and Europe/London. Uses `zoneinfo`; "now" is injected
  so tests control the clock.

## Notes

There is no real push notification. `next_nudge(user, nights, now)` returns
`Nudge(at, silent, text)` and the page shows "Your next wind-down nudge: 22:15".
# BR-07: Support a consistent wind-down routine

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | Business requirement |
| Owner | Product (fictional: Priya N., Head of Product) |
| Status | Approved |
| Refined by | [PR-21](PR-21.md) |

## Need

People who keep a regular bedtime routine report feeling more rested. NightJar
should help users build a consistent wind-down routine around the time they
normally go to bed, without making any medical or treatment claims.

## Success measure

- 30% of active users with 7+ logged nights keep their bedtime within 30 minutes
  of their usual bedtime on 5 of 7 nights, after 4 weeks.

## Constraints

- Wellness only. All user-facing copy must follow the [claims register](../claims.md).
- Works for users who travel or live through daylight-saving changes.

content.text:
# Edge cases to check for S-116 (weekly sleep summary)

I read S-116 and the docs it depends on: S-114 (the nudge), BR-07 and the claims policy.

## AC1: the seven-night window
- **Window boundaries.** "Seven days ago up to and including last night" is 7 night-of dates. The nights are today−7 through today−1, which is 7 dates if you count both ends. Confirm that's the intent. Check that a night on the today−7 date is included, a night on today−8 is excluded, and tonight or today's date is excluded.
- **After-midnight bedtimes.** A 00:15 bedtime on Sunday counts as the Saturday night. Check this at the window edges too. A 00:15 bedtime on today (which belongs to last night) is in. A 00:15 bedtime on the today−7 date, which belongs to the night of today−8, is out.
- **Time zone for "today".** "Today" uses the user's current time zone. Check the window when the user has just changed zones. Check around local midnight, when "today" differs between the old and new zones. Check a user who has moved across the date line.
- **Ambiguous "night of" assignment.** Check a nap or a daytime sleep, and a bedtime between 12:00 and 18:00. The story doesn't say which date these belong to.
- **Multiple entries on the same night.** Check two logs for one night-of date, such as a wake-up and then a second sleep. The story doesn't say whether they count as one night or two. This affects "nights logged", the average and the median.
- **Duplicate or overlapping entries.** Check the same night logged twice, and overlapping entries.
- **Edited or deleted nights.** Check that the summary reflects a night edited or deleted after it was first shown.

## AC2: figures and counts
- **Count versus window.** The count must be the number of nights logged in the window, never more than 7. Entries outside the window must not leak in.
- **Zero nights.** Check an empty diary and a brand-new user. This should show the AC5 message, not "0 nights" or a division by zero.

## AC3: average time asleep
- **Rounding.** "Nearest 5 minutes" needs a rule for exact midpoints. Test 7 h 27 min 30 s, 7 h 22 min 30 s and 2 min 29 s versus 2 min 30 s, and say whether halves round up or to even. Check what happens when rounding gives 60 minutes: 7 h 58 min should show "8 h 0 min" (or "8 h"), not "7 h 60 min". Check how 0 minutes is formatted, such as "8 h 0 min" versus "8 h". Check an average under 1 hour, for example "0 h 45 min" versus "45 min". Check sub-minute precision, because seconds in the data could change the rounding.
- **Mean not median.** Use a data set where mean and median differ, so a wrong implementation is caught.
- **Very short and very long nights.** Check a 0-minute night, a 20-hour night and an implausible entry. Check whether bad data is capped or excluded.
- **Display text.** The format is "7 h 25 min" with a non-breaking or regular space. Check that it matches the format exactly.

## AC4: usual bedtime (the highest-risk area)
- **Median across midnight.** Bedtimes of 23:30 and 00:30 are one hour apart. For example, 23:00, 23:30, 00:30 should give 23:30. A naive median of clock times gives the wrong answer.
- **Midnight itself.** Check bedtimes exactly at 00:00, a set that straddles 12:00, and a set spread evenly around the clock.
- **Even number of nights.** Check a median of 4, 5 or 6 nights. The two middle values need an averaging rule, which has to work across midnight and to a defined precision. For example, the median of 23:50 and 00:10 should be 00:00, not 12:00.
- **Same rule as the nudge.** The story says to handle bedtimes "as they are for the nudge". Test that the summary and S-114 `sleep_window.py` give the same answer for the same inputs, and ideally share the code.
- **Each night in its own time zone.** Check a user who travelled mid-week, so bedtimes were logged in different zones. Check the same wall-clock bedtime in two zones. Check that it's the local time at logging that is used, not the current zone.
- **DST on the bedtime.** Check a bedtime that falls in the skipped hour (a local time that doesn't exist) or the repeated hour (an ambiguous local time). Check this in America/Toronto and Europe/London, the zones S-114 uses.
- **Display.** Check the 12-hour versus 24-hour format and rounding to the minute (or to 5 minutes?). The story doesn't say how the usual bedtime is shown.

## AC5: fewer than 3 nights
- **Threshold.** Test 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 nights. Exactly 3 must show figures. Exactly 2 must show the message.
- **Qualifying nights.** Check 3 logged entries where one falls outside the window, so only 2 count. Check 3 entries for the same night, which is 1 night. This case needs the answer to the multiple-entries question above.
- **No figures at all.** With 2 nights, the count, the average and the bedtime must all be hidden. Check that "2 nights logged" doesn't appear.
- **Exact wording.** Check the text "Log at least 3 nights this week to see your summary." character for character, including the full stop. Note the "this week" wording is slightly misleading, because the window is the last 7 days rather than a calendar week.

## AC6: the claims check
- **All copy goes through `claims.check_text`.** This includes labels, the AC5 message, any headings and any "nice job" style text.
- **False positives.** The check is deliberately strict. Words like "treat", and anything near "insomnia", "diagnose" or "cure", are flagged. Check that nothing in the summary wording trips it. Watch for casual phrases such as "Treat yourself".
